- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, particularly in early horizon.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.85–0.95 multiplier) to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- In 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture downward trend after sentiment shifts to negative; add 1–2% downward bias if sentiment drops below 0.3 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+1.00” followed by “-1.00”, model tends to overcorrect; apply 0.9–0.95 correction to subsequent forecasts.
